Important: if pure shellable Δ and Δ∪2^F both shellable (indeed CM) of dim d, then Δ∩2^F must be pure dim d−1 (Depth Lemma / CM union), so any shelling of Δ appends F. Thus b(d,k≥d)=0 really equivalent Simon extendability, not weakened by allowing shelling reorder. Likely recent negative Simon result needed; seek abstract obstruction.

Useful general lemma: every k-decomp complex admits an ordering of its facets with all prefixes k-decomp (induct on shedding decomposition; add deletion facets then σ*link facets according to prefix order of link). Apex lifting idea: C=Δ∪a*Γ initially Γ=skel_{d−1}Δ. If Γ grows by shelling facet R with restriction τ (τ not in Γ), then C gains aR with same restriction τ (all Δ lower faces⊂Γ). So shellable extension of Γ lifts to shellable extension C. Once Γ full old skeleton, all old missing facets attach full boundary. Thus for shellability b(d,d)≤b(d−1,d)+1, base d=1→ b≤d−1 (or d−2 if Simon d2 known). For k-decomp need generalized lifting preserving decomposition, not merely restrictions.

Rigorous direct append lemma avoiding CM: if Δ and Δ+F pure shellable d, and maximal H=Δ∩2^F face T has |T|≤d−1, then lk_T(Δ+F)=lk_TΔ ∪ 2^(F\T), disjoint vertex sets since T maximal H. Both nonempty, link dimension ≥1, hence disconnected, contradict shellability links. So H pure codim1 and every shelling of Δ appends F. Exact exhaustive code saved workspace/agent4_checks.py, executed k1/2/3 d3,n6, 18153 decomposable each, no noncompletable.

Exploring shellable neighborly 3-spheres: a missing tetra F is shelling-addable iff ≥3 of its triangles already present (all edges present). Thus any neighborly shellable sphere with no empty tetra having 3 or 4 triangles obstructs. This is no decreasing 3→2 bistellar move/no missing tetra. Such 'unflippable' spheres may exist but shellability likely excludes known examples. n≤9 counting forces addable; n=10 boundary case all missing exactly2 triangles.

For smaller k, same cone step need not preserve k-decomp because del_a acquires unsupported lower faces.

Strong reservoir lemma: Any pure d-complex consisting of ALL d-facets containing fixed apex a plus an ARBITRARY selection of old d-facets is vertex-decomposable. Delete any old vertex v; deletion and link have same form in dim d / d−1, and purity follows from full apex star (base n=d+1 gives simplex/boundary cases). Thus after full a-star is built, all remaining old facets can be added preserving even vertex-decomp, independent of k.

Need pure dimension≥q terminal with no free q-faces obtainable by q-free-face removals from initial dual. This likely explains why standard contractible noncollapsible examples don't settle it.
